questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dr. K.M. Munshi, a member of the Drafting Committee, described the Preamble of the Indian Constitution as "The Political Horoscope of our Constitution."
2. Sir Ernest Barker referred to the Preamble as the "Identity card of the Constitution."
questions.solution:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
  • K.M. Munshi: "Political Horoscope."
  • N.A. Palkhiwala: Referred to it as the "Identity card."
  • Sir Ernest Barker: Referred to it as the "Keynote."

questions.question: When was the preamble to the Indian Constitution amended?
questions.solution: The Preamble has been amended only once, in 1976, by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act.

questions.question: When is Constitution Day observed in India?
questions.solution: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed on 26 November to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution in 1949.

questions.question: Who among the following is called 'Father of Indian constitution'?
questions.solution: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution due to his monumental role as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the designer of India’s National Flag:
i. Pingali Venkayya presented the original design of the Indian flag with red and green colors to Mahatma Gandhi in 1921.
ii. The National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India on 22 July 1947.
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Pingali Venkayya designed the flag, and it was officially adopted by the Assembly on July 22, 1947, just before independence.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities was appointed as the legal advisor of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the document of the Constitution?
questions.solution: Sir B.N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional/Legal Advisor to the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The original Constitution of India was handwritten in English by Prem Behari Narayan Raizada in a flowing italic style.
2. The original Indian Constitution consisted of 117,369 words and 251 pages.
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The original document was not printed or typed; it was beautifully calligraphed by Prem Behari Narayan Raizada in English.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities was the chief draftsman of the constituent assembly that drafted the document of the Constitution?
questions.solution: S.N. Mukherjee was the Chief Draftsman of the Constitution in the Constituent Assembly. (Note: Do not confuse this with the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, who was Dr. Ambedkar).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Hindi version of the original Indian Constitution was written in calligraphic style by Vasant Krishan Vaidya.
2. Artists from Shantiniketan, including Nand Lal Bose and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha, decorated and beautified the original Constitution.
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. While Raizada did the English calligraphy, Vasant Krishan Vaidya did the Hindi version. The artistic decorations were handled by Nand Lal Bose and his team from Shantiniketan.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The structural part of the Indian Constitution is largely derived from the Government of India Act, 1935.
2. The Act provided for the division of powers between the Centre and units through the Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent Lists.
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. About 60-70% of the Constitution's structure comes from the 1935 Act, including the three-list system of power distribution.

questions.question: Which is NOT a unitary feature of the Constitution of India?
questions.option_4: Appointment of the Governor by the President
questions.solution: Bicameral Legislature (having two houses like Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) is a federal feature, as the upper house (Rajya Sabha) represents the states. The other options (Integrated Judiciary, Single Citizenship, and Appointment of Governors) are unitary features that strengthen the Centre.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Division of powers, written constitution, and independent judiciary are federal features of the Indian Constitution.
2. All India Services is a federal feature of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
  • Federal Features: Written constitution, Supremacy of Constitution, Division of powers, Independent judiciary, Bicameralism.
  • Unitary Features: All India Services (IAS, IPS), Single citizenship, Strong Centre, Appointment of Governor.

questions.question: With reference to the Constituent Assembly, which of the following statements is Correct?
questions.option_1: The Constituent Assembly ratified India’s membership of the Commonwealth in May 1947.
questions.option_2: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Anthem in January 1950.
questions.option_3: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Song in January 1948.
questions.option_4: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag in July 1949.
questions.solution:
Statement 2 is correct.
  • National Anthem & Song: Both adopted on 24 January 1950.
  • National Flag: Adopted on 22 July 1947.
  • Commonwealth Membership: Ratified in May 1949.

questions.question: How many female members were part of the Constituent Assembly that framed the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: There were 15 female members in the Constituent Assembly, including notable figures like Sarojini Naidu, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, and Vijayalakshmi Pandit.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
questions.option_1: B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was the Chairman of the House Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India.
questions.option_2: AV Thakkar was the founder of the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan in 1938.
questions.option_3: J.B. Kripalani was the President of the Indian National Congress during Independence.
questions.option_4: K.M. Munshi served as Minister for Agriculture & Food (1952–53).
questions.solution: Statement 2 is incorrect. The founder of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan was K.M. Munshi in 1938. A.V. Thakkar (Thakkar Bapa) is known for founding the Bhil Seva Mandal in 1922.

questions.question: GV Mavalankar was the Chairman of the ______ of the Constituent Assembly of India.
questions.option_1: Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas
questions.option_4: Ad hoc Committee on the National Flag
questions.solution: G.V. Mavalankar was the Chairman of the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly. He later became the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The total membership of the Constituent Assembly was 389.
2. Out of this, 93 members represented the princely states.
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The original strength was 389: 292 from British provinces, 93 from princely states, and 4 from chief commissioner provinces.

questions.question: The members of the Constituent Assembly signed the Constitution of India on ______.
questions.solution: The Constitution of India was signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950. This was the final meeting of the Assembly where the document, containing 395 Articles, 8 Schedules, and 22 Parts, was formally accepted by all members.

questions.question: In which year did Motilal Nehru (Chairman) and eight other Congress leaders draft a constitution for India?
questions.solution: In 1928, a committee headed by Motilal Nehru drafted a constitution known as the Nehru Report. This initiative was a response to Lord Birkenhead, the Secretary of State for India, who challenged Indian leaders to produce a constitutional scheme that was acceptable to all sections of Indian society.

questions.question:
Which constitutional features in India are linked to the Australian Constitution?
A) Freedom of trade and commerce
B) Joint sitting of the two Houses
C) Federal structure with strong Centre
D) Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.solution:
The features borrowed from the Australian Constitution are Freedom of trade and commerce and the Joint sitting of the two Houses (Article 108).
Note: The 'Federal structure with a strong Centre' and 'Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court' were borrowed from the Canadian Constitution.

questions.question: The concept of "Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)" in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
questions.solution: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), found in Part IV (Articles 36–51), were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (1937). These are non-justiciable guidelines aimed at creating a social and economic democracy and establishing a welfare state.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Republic feature of the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the French Constitution.
2. Ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity in the Preamble are also taken from the French Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The concepts of a Republic and the ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity mentioned in our Preamble were inspired by the French Revolution and borrowed from the French Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutions inspired the law-making process in India?
questions.solution: The law-making process (legislative procedure) and the Parliamentary system were inspired by the British Constitution. Other British influences include the Rule of Law, Single Citizenship, Cabinet System, and Bicameralism.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The concept of ‘Independence of Judiciary’ in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.
2. Fundamental Rights and the process of impeachment of the President are also borrowed from the USA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The United States provided the foundation for the Independence of Judiciary, Judicial Review, Fundamental Rights, and the procedure for the impeachment of the President.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Constitution adopted the ‘First Past the Post’ system from the American Constitution.
2. In the FPTP system, the candidate with the highest votes is declared elected even without an absolute majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Only Statement 2 is correct.
  • Statement 1: The First Past the Post (FPTP) system was actually borrowed from the British (UK) Constitution, not the American one.
  • Statement 2: In this system, the candidate who receives more votes than any other candidate wins the seat, regardless of whether they have a majority (50% + 1) of the total votes.
